name: lifecycle_debug_decision_inverted
why: Debug leg (explain-only): containment fired on the wrong alerts. Inherits the inverted-decision broken playbook. Graded on whether the diagnosis names the real defect -- the reputation gate's comparison is backwards (routes to block when the score is BELOW the threshold, not above), so malicious IPs take the default arm and clean ones get blocked -- a routing-logic defect, not a parameter or loop one. Graded on the diagnosis, not on reaching a diagnostic tool.
goal: This phishing playbook ran on the box and reported success, but it blocked the wrong alerts -- malicious sender IPs went through untouched while a couple of clean ones were quarantined. Explain WHY. Do not change the playbook, just tell me the cause.
defect: The reputation gate's comparison is backwards -- it routes to the block when reputation is below 50 (< 50) instead of above 50 (> 50) -- so malicious high-reputation IPs take the clean default arm and clean low-reputation ones get blocked.
